newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan launches check on stock credit trading.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan launches check on stock credit trading.

text.p: Taiwan's Securities & Futures Commission said on Wednesday it had launched a routine investigation on credit trading in the stock market, but denied the move was aimed to dampen the recently red hot stock market.
"We checked 15 local securities brokerages on Tuesday to see if there is any violation in the procedures of intraday credit trading," Chen Wei-lung, a commission deputy director, told Reuters.
"This is a routine check. It's not a move to dampen the market," Chen said.
Taiwan's stock index has surged some 12 percent since late May, and turnover has expanded significantly, hitting an all-time-high T$251 billion on Thursday.
On Tuesday, Taiwan's index ended down 6.95 points or 0.08 percent at 8,918.17, reflecting Wall Street's Monday plunge.
Chen said credit trading -- including margin loan buying and short selling -- had accounted for some 55 percent of the market's daily turnover recently.
"And intraday credit trading had accounted for 25-30 percent of credit trading, indicating speculation is strengthening," Chen said.
"The check is to see whether intraday trading in these brokerages had followed rules, so as to avoid speculation."
But he declined to release the results of the checking.
"We don't usually release the checking results, but if there are any serious violations, we may announce the results in later days," Chen said.
